record.original_question: Are there constructions that build (n+1)-polytopes from n-polytopes and produce symmetry type graphs not obtainable from the standard Theorem 4.2 construction of attaching semi-edges at every vertex, and not obtainable from those graphs by duality?

evidence.quote: Problem 13. Are there constructions of (n + 1)-polytopes P from n-polytopes where the symmetry type graph of P is different from those in Theorem 4.2 and from their duals?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a graded poset (with proper elements of ranks 0,…,n−1) satisfying the standard diamond, flag-connectedness, and strong flag-connectedness conditions for abstract polytopes. The automorphism group Γ(P) of an abstract polytope P acts on the set of flags of P, and the quotient of the flag graph of P by this action (with edges labeled by ranks 0,…,n−1 and with semi-edges where a flag is fixed by the corresponding adjacency) is called the symmetry type graph T(P) of P. A "rank-raising construction" is a procedure that, given an abstract n-polytope Q, produces an abstract (n+1)-polytope P whose symmetry type graph T(P) is determined by T(Q).

One standard rank-raising construction yields T(P) from T(Q) by attaching a semi-edge of label n at every vertex of T(Q) (so that, in particular, every flag of P is fixed by the rank-n adjacency). Dualizing P (which has the effect on T(P) of reversing all rank labels via i ↦ n−i) gives another family of symmetry type graphs obtainable from T(Q).

Problem. Does there exist a construction taking an abstract n-polytope Q to an abstract (n+1)-polytope P such that the symmetry type graph T(P) is neither of the form produced by the semi-edge-attachment construction above applied to T(Q), nor the dual of such a graph?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on k-orbit polytopes and symmetry type graphs (including work on 2-orbit maniplexes, 3-orbit polyhedra, voltage-graph constructions, and prescribing symmetries) continues to develop rank-raising and related constructions, but no source found explicitly settles whether every (n+1)-polytope's symmetry type graph arising from an n-polytope can be obtained from the standard semi-edge construction or its dual. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Polytopality of 2-orbit maniplexes
status_evidence.snippet: Studies symmetry-type graphs and constructions of polytopes with prescribed flag-orbit structure.
status_evidence.claim: Active research on constructions of polytopes from symmetry type graphs continues without resolving this specific rank-raising question.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on group-theoretic characterizations rather than rank-raising symmetry-type-graph constructions.

status_evidence.title: Symmetry Type Graphs of Polytopes and Maniplexes
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces symmetry type graphs as quotients of flag graphs by automorphism actions.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the framework but does not resolve the rank-raising question.
